description: Canonical universal mythological themes, archetypal patterns, biblical bridges, and modern parallels for the PÚNYCODEX AI synthesis corpus.

themes.label: Creation from Chaos
themes.description: The cosmos emerges from an undifferentiated primordial state—void, waters, darkness, or a singular egg—through the action of a generative force.
themes.archetypal_summary: Before form there is formlessness; order crystallizes from disorder, echoing the perennial experience of potential preceding actuality.

themes.label: Primordial Waters
themes.description: The pre-creation universe is conceived as a vast watery abyss from which land, sky, and life are separated or born.
themes.archetypal_summary: Water as the universal matrix—formless, fertile, and prior to distinction—mirrors the unconscious and the undifferentiated ground of being.

themes.label: Cosmic Egg
themes.description: The universe or a creator deity hatches from an egg, symbolizing latent totality before differentiation.
themes.archetypal_summary: The egg encloses all opposites in potentia; its breaking is the first act of cosmogenesis and the birth of duality.

themes.label: Axis Mundi / World Tree
themes.description: A central axis—tree, mountain, or pillar—connects the underworld, earth, and sky, stabilizing the cosmos.
themes.archetypal_summary: The axis mundi is the spine of reality, a bridge between realms and a symbol of centeredness and spiritual ascent.

themes.label: Solar Deity
themes.description: A god or goddess embodying the sun, often associated with sovereignty, sight, justice, and the triumph of light over darkness.
themes.archetypal_summary: The sun is the visible face of cosmic order, the eye that sees all and the force that sustains life and time.

themes.label: Lunar Deity
themes.description: A deity governing the moon, cycles, dreams, the tides, feminine mysteries, and the liminal spaces between worlds.
themes.archetypal_summary: The moon governs becoming and dissolution, reflection and intuition, marking the rhythm of bodies and ecosystems.

themes.label: Sky Father
themes.description: A sovereign male deity of the sky, rain, thunder, and kingship, often paired with an earth mother.
themes.archetypal_summary: The sky father projects law, distance, and authority; he is the canopy of order above the fertile ground.

themes.label: Earth Mother
themes.description: A generative female deity of the land, fertility, agriculture, and the cycles of birth and decay.
themes.archetypal_summary: The earth mother is the body that receives, nourishes, and reclaims; she is the ground of all terrestrial becoming.

themes.label: Storm & Thunder Deity
themes.description: A powerful deity who wields lightning, thunder, and rain, often a warrior-king or divine judge.
themes.archetypal_summary: The storm god is sudden, decisive power—judgment carved in light across the sky, bringing both terror and fertilizing rain.

themes.label: Descent to the Underworld
themes.description: A deity or hero travels to the realm of the dead, confronting mortality, shadows, and the hidden aspects of existence.
themes.archetypal_summary: Descent myths map the necessary confrontation with what lies beneath consciousness: grief, transformation, and the retrieval of lost value.

themes.label: Death & Rebirth
themes.description: A figure dies, dismembers, or descends and returns transformed, often bringing renewal to the world.
themes.archetypal_summary: Death and rebirth is the pattern of initiation—ego dissolution followed by reintegration at a higher order of being.

themes.label: Vegetation & Harvest Deity
themes.description: A deity tied to grain, vines, seasons, and agricultural abundance, whose fate mirrors the planting and reaping cycle.
themes.archetypal_summary: The vegetation god embodies the covenant between human labor and natural fertility, teaching that life feeds on death.

themes.label: Trickster
themes.description: A boundary-crossing figure who disrupts order, steals fire or secrets, and often becomes the accidental creator of culture.
themes.archetypal_summary: The trickster is the shadow of order, exposing its limits and opening the door to novelty through transgression.

themes.label: Culture Hero
themes.description: A figure who brings fire, writing, agriculture, laws, or medicine to humanity, often suffering for the gift.
themes.archetypal_summary: The culture hero carries the Promethean spark: knowledge gained at cost, lifting humanity from animal immediacy into symbolic life.

themes.label: Wisdom & Knowledge
themes.description: A deity or sage embodying insight, writing, magic, prophecy, and the ordering power of mind.
themes.archetypal_summary: Wisdom deities teach that perception is creative: to name, measure, and remember is to participate in cosmic order.

themes.label: Love, Desire & Beauty
themes.description: A deity governing erotic love, beauty, attraction, and the binding force that draws beings together.
themes.archetypal_summary: Love deities reveal attraction as a cosmological principle: the pull that creates bonds, families, artworks, and conflicts.

themes.label: War & Conflict
themes.description: A deity embodying battle, strategy, rage, and the terrible necessity of armed struggle.
themes.archetypal_summary: War gods externalize the martial drive in nature and society, showing conflict as both destruction and crucible of honor.

themes.label: Fate, Time & Necessity
themes.description: Deities or forces that spin, measure, and cut the thread of life, representing inevitability and cosmic timing.
themes.archetypal_summary: Fate personifies the sense that life has pattern beyond individual will—an ancient intuition of causal networks and temporal irreversibility.
modern_parallels: entropy and the arrow of time

themes.label: Magic, Sorcery & the Hidden Arts
themes.description: A deity, witch, or sorcerer who commands hidden forces, transformation, and the language of power.
themes.archetypal_summary: Magic is the art of influencing reality through symbol, will, and affinity—a precursor to both technology and psychotherapy.

themes.label: Sacred King & Sacrificial God
themes.description: A divine or semi-divine king whose life, death, and renewal guarantees the fertility and order of the realm.
themes.archetypal_summary: The sacred king concentrates collective destiny in one body; his sacrifice renews the social and natural order.

themes.label: Hero & Monster-Slayer
themes.description: A mortal or demigod who undertakes impossible labors, slays monsters, and returns with a boon for society.
themes.archetypal_summary: The hero's journey encodes the necessary ego-death and transformation required to individuate and serve the collective.

themes.label: The Flood & Cosmic Deluge
themes.description: A universal flood myth in which the divine punishes or resets humanity, while a chosen few survive to repopulate the world.
themes.archetypal_summary: The flood is the psyche's experience of overwhelming change—destruction that is also purification and new beginning.

themes.label: Divine Twins & Dioscuri
themes.description: A pair of siblings—often one mortal, one divine—representing complementary forces such as light/dark, war/peace, or sky/earth.
themes.archetypal_summary: The divine twins express the tension and union of opposites, a recurring structure in Indo-European and global myth.

themes.label: Light versus Darkness
themes.description: A cosmic struggle between luminous order and shadowy chaos, often personified as rival deities or primordial siblings.
themes.archetypal_summary: Light and darkness are not merely moral poles but complementary phases of a single cycle; their conflict generates visible reality.

themes.label: Law, Order & Cosmic Truth
themes.description: A principle or deity establishing truth, justice, righteousness, and the regularities that make civilization possible.
themes.archetypal_summary: Cosmic law is the discovery that existence has pattern; to align with it is maat, rta, asha, or dharma.

themes.label: Cosmic Combat & Dragon-Slaying
themes.description: A creator god battles and defeats a primordial monster—dragon, serpent, or chaos-beast—to establish the ordered world.
themes.archetypal_summary: The chaoskampf is the archetype of order emerging through decisive struggle with the unformed depths.
